races.name: Watch On Racing TV Juvenile Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Sudbury Hill
runners_data.note: Progressive juvenile hurdler for Harry Derham who arrives just six days after a runner-up finish over 17f on Good ground, giving him strong recency and proven stamina; his hold-up style is entirely genuine here and the even, uncontested pace set by Wicksey should set him up for his natural late challenge.

runners_data.name: Tiny Riot
runners_data.note: Dan Skelton's charge showed a sharp improvement to win over 16f on Good going 17 days ago and Harry Skelton's booking is significant; a genuine hold-up runner whose profile — two runs, two strong finishes — suits a race run at a controlled pace where he can deploy his turn of foot late.

runners_data.name: Lucky Sevens
runners_data.note: Won impressively over 10f on Good ground and clearly has ability, but in truth he races in a come-from-behind style and has been pushed into a midfield map position because the hold-up berths are occupied; his STYLE_FIT score (0.92) reflects that he is unlikely to race in his ideal position, which tempers confidence in his finishing effort.

runners_data.name: Serragasso
runners_data.note: Clare Hobson's runner arrives on an extended break of 95 days and brings only flat form over sprint trips on Standard artificial surfaces, making this a significant step into the unknown; a natural hold-up type mapped to midfield, he also carries a noted tendency to fade in the finish — both factors combine to make him the most speculative runner in the field.

runners_data.name: Wicksey
runners_data.note: Ben Haslam's sole confirmed pace-setter has won three times including over hurdles, but his STYLE_FIT tag (0.93) suggests the prominent role is slightly stretched; his four-run hurdles record shows one win on Standard and a runner-up on Good, and the absence of any rival to push him means the quality of his jumping will determine whether he can be caught.

runners_data.name: High Aura
runners_data.note: The Skelton second string is completely unknown from a hurdles perspective — no rating history and no hurdles form is available — making her wholly unquantifiable; the trainer's current 14-day form (12/30) provides the only positive angle, and Tristan Durrell's conditional allowance may be a secondary factor on Good to Firm ground.

races.paceDynamic: Wicksey is the only confirmed front-runner in this six-runner juvenile hurdle and will stride into a clear lead from the outset on Good to Firm ground at Stratford, setting a sustainable and uncontested tempo that rewards those who can travel smoothly in behind. The field holds more hold-up types than the race map can accommodate at the rear — Serragasso and Lucky Sevens are genuine come-from-behind horses in their flat profiles but have been redistributed to midfield, meaning the true rearward positions will be occupied by Sudbury Hill and Tiny Riot, who are the authentic hold-up runners here. With a single pace-setter dictating a controlled gallop, the race shape strongly favours hold-up horses with a high cruising speed who can close off a true end-to-end gallop — specifically Sudbury Hill and Tiny Riot, both of whom have the form, jockey profile and hurdling experience to deliver a late challenge on a track that will be quick underfoot.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Wicksey Controls, Closers Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If Wicksey dictates an uncontested lead at a fair but not punishing pace and hold-up horses track in behind before producing sustained late runs.
scenarios.body: If Wicksey dictates an uncontested lead at a fair but not punishing pace and hold-up horses track in behind before producing sustained late runs.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Wicksey Steals It Wire-To-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Wicksey's prompt lead becomes a front-running theft and the chasers fail to close the gap through the final two hurdles.
scenarios.body: If Wicksey's prompt lead becomes a front-running theft and the chasers fail to close the gap through the final two hurdles.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Trio Clash, Race Fragments
scenarios.trigger: If Lucky Sevens and Serragasso both push forward despite their redistribution and create a more contested early pace alongside Wicksey.
scenarios.body: If Lucky Sevens and Serragasso both push forward despite their redistribution and create a more contested early pace alongside Wicksey.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete Outsider Scenario
scenarios.trigger: If High Aura — the unknown quantity with no hurdles form on record — produces an unexpectedly polished round of jumping and benefits from the steady pace.
scenarios.body: If High Aura — the unknown quantity with no hurdles form on record — produces an unexpectedly polished round of jumping and benefits from the steady pace.

watchPoints.text: Wicksey's jumping under pressure — if he makes a significant error at a hurdle while in front uncontested, the entire race shape collapses and the hold-up horses behind him may be inconvenienced or gifted a winning opportunity.

Watch whether Lucky Sevens or Serragasso push forward against their natural hold-up inclinations in the early stages; either doing so could create an unexpected injection of pace and compromise Wicksey's clean lead.

Serragasso's noted tendency to fade in the finish combined with her long layoff (95 days) and sprint flat background makes her a live danger of weakening at a critical point — horses racing close behind her should be monitored if she backs off the hurdle.

High Aura's debut round of jumping is the single biggest unknown in the race — a fluent, confident round from this Dan Skelton juvenile on fast ground could bring her into contention without warning, while a novice error could end her challenge instantly.

Sudbury Hill's rider Josh Williamson is a 5lb claimer — on a quick surface over hurdles, any positional error or delayed manoeuvre in a small field could cost ground that a hold-up horse cannot afford to give away at this distance.

runners_data.name: Juan Bermudez
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner here, last won over this course and distance on good ground, trainer Henry Oliver in a lean spell (0/5 in 14 days), but the uncontested lead is a substantial tactical gift that offsets form concerns; tongue-strap noted.

runners_data.name: Katherine
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old hold-up mare whose recent form reads poorly (eighth last time), trainer Adrian Sexton 0/10 in past fortnight, and she has not won off the back of a prominent position in years; the good-to-firm surface is fine but a lack of a strong finishing effort makes her difficult to enthuse about.

runners_data.name: Uhtred Ragnarson
runners_data.note: Alan King's five-year-old is a natural hold-up horse and the trainer has been in form (2/29 over 14 days), last seen finishing seventh but with winning form on good going at a shorter trip; the step up to two and a half miles on quick ground is the live question, though his close-up finishing style is the sort this pace map rewards.

runners_data.name: Pahlavi
runners_data.note: John Joseph Hanlon's nine-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse whose natural position is at the rear — mapped to midfield here because the whole field shares that profile — and his recent form (5, 6, 11 from his last three) gives little encouragement, though the sim-going score (14/15) confirms the surface is not a concern.

runners_data.name: Reteti
runners_data.note: Sheena West's six-year-old has a sound profile on similar ground (sim-going 10/15) and consistent placed form from the back, all four recent placed efforts coming in hold-up fashion at shorter; the natural style suits a strong-galloping race but the pace here may be too moderate to fully illuminate his finishing kick.

runners_data.name: Playful Fox
runners_data.note: Harry Skelton takes over on this Dan Skelton-trained four-year-old, and the trainer's 14-day record of 11/26 is the standout yard stat in the field; a genuine hold-up type whose two recent wins came on good ground, and Skelton's ability to judge pace from off it makes him the most tactically dangerous of the closers despite the style-fit caveat.

races.paceDynamic: Juan Bermudez is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will dictate at whatever tempo suits him on good-to-firm ground at Stratford over two and a half miles. Lilly Pinchin can set a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front, and without any rival willing to press him, the fractions are likely to be measured rather than punishing — creating a race that develops late rather than one that shakes out early. Katherine, Uhtred Ragnarson, Pahlavi, Reteti, and Playful Fox are all hold-up types by nature, meaning the field will be strung out behind Bermudez with the closers forced to make ground on a horse who has never truly been tested by another front-runner in this contest. This race shape decisively favours prominent and hold-up horses who can travel fluently, reach Juan Bermudez early in the straight, and sustain a run on quick ground — Juan Bermudez himself is the primary beneficiary of an uncontested lead, but hold-up horses with a strong late gear are the likeliest challengers if the gallop proves too easy and he stops in front.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Bermudez Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Juan Bermudez leads at a controlled pace and none of the hold-up field can close down the deficit in the straight.
scenarios.body: If Juan Bermudez leads at a controlled pace and none of the hold-up field can close down the deficit in the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely fast enough to leave Bermudez vulnerable and a hold-up horse produces a powerful late run.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely fast enough to leave Bermudez vulnerable and a hold-up horse produces a powerful late run.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Bermudez Fades, Group Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Juan Bermudez sets too strong an early gallop relative to his fitness and flattens out turning for home.
scenarios.body: If Juan Bermudez sets too strong an early gallop relative to his fitness and flattens out turning for home.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Scrappy Contested Finish
scenarios.trigger: If several hold-up horses commit earlier than their natural style demands and crowd the straight, creating a messy blanket finish.
scenarios.body: If several hold-up horses commit earlier than their natural style demands and crowd the straight, creating a messy blanket finish.

watchPoints.text: Juan Bermudez's lead goes uncontested — watch whether Lilly Pinchin exploits this ruthlessly from the front or settles for a comfortable rhythm that invites challengers late.

Playful Fox with Harry Skelton is the most dangerous hold-up horse in the field; watch whether Skelton tracks Bermudez more closely than his natural style would suggest, effectively switching the race shape mid-contest.

Uhtred Ragnarson's stamina for the extra distance at this pace is unproven — watch his jumping and travelling in the final mile as an indicator of whether his hold-up style can translate over two and a half miles on fast ground.

Pahlavi and Reteti are both genuine rear-runners mapped to midfield due to the cluster of hold-up types — if either is seen tracking prominently from early on, that would represent a genuine riding change worth noting for the scenario read.

races.name: Sun Racing The Home Of Racing Novices' Handicap Chase

runners_data.name: Catchim
runners_data.note: Hold-up racer with solid course form at this trip on good ground, trained by the Pogsons who have had a quiet recent spell (0/4 in 14 days); finished third and won at this distance in similar conditions, but needs a stronger-than-expected gallop to land a blow from the rear.

runners_data.name: A Little Something
runners_data.note: Back-to-back winner over 2m on good ground for Emma Lavelle, she slots in here as the confirmed pace-setter at a slightly longer trip than her recent wins; her natural prominence is a style fit for the front, not a liability, and Ben Jones has ridden her to both recent victories.

runners_data.name: White Riot
runners_data.note: Prominent type for Fergal O'Brien whose yard is in fair nick (3/25 in 14 days); has a fall in recent form which must be noted, but his one win came at 2m on good ground and he maps naturally just off the leader — jumping safely is the key condition here.

runners_data.name: Gore Point
runners_data.note: Consistent placed horse who has finished second on three of his last five starts, all on good or good-to-firm ground; Sam Twiston-Davies takes the ride and this type of patient prominent hold could suit, with the tongue tie applied for the first time adding a small unknown.

runners_data.name: Kings Order
runners_data.note: Lightly weighted hold-up runner who has failed to place in six of his last seven starts; going form is acceptable but his record on good ground is thin and nothing in his recent history suggests he can land a blow from the back at this level.

runners_data.name: No Mean Feat
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse in terms of natural racing style, shifted into a midfield mapping position here because the field is congested at the rear; returning after 54 days off and fitted with a hood, his form figures show consistency in placing but no wins and his out-of-role mapping tempers expectations.

runners_data.name: Citizen Jane
runners_data.note: Has won twice from a hold-up position but all five of her most recent runs have come on soft ground, making the good-to-firm conditions a significant query; absent for 807 days before a recent run and mapped into midfield due to redistribution, her natural style is further back than shown — the going and long layoff are the primary concerns.

races.paceDynamic: A Little Something is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival willing to challenge from the front, she is set to establish a comfortable, unhurried lead on good-to-firm ground over 2m3½f at Stratford. Gore Point, White Riot, and potentially Citizen Jane and No Mean Feat all carry prominent or hold-up tendencies, but the field contains more horses wanting to race handy than the map can accommodate — A Little Something is overwhelmingly most likely to secure the lead, with Gore Point and White Riot the likeliest to fill the prominent berths behind her. The result is a sustainable, controlled gallop with A Little Something dictating from the front and the hold-up horses — Catchim and Kings Order — forced to make up ground on a track that rewards those who travel economically close to the pace. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can sit just off the pace and pounce in the straight, and horses with good finishing kicks are disadvantaged by a lack of truly pressured early fractions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If A Little Something is allowed to dictate a sustainable gallop from the front and no rival applies early pressure.
scenarios.body: If A Little Something is allowed to dictate a sustainable gallop from the front and no rival applies early pressure.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Chaser Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If A Little Something weakens in the final half-mile and a prominent stalker overhauls her on the run-in.
scenarios.body: If A Little Something weakens in the final half-mile and a prominent stalker overhauls her on the run-in.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Gets Home
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to string the field out and a closer can make late ground count on good-to-firm turf.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to string the field out and a closer can make late ground count on good-to-firm turf.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On Alone
scenarios.trigger: If no rival gets close enough to threaten A Little Something and she wins with more in hand than the pace scenario suggests.
scenarios.body: If no rival gets close enough to threaten A Little Something and she wins with more in hand than the pace scenario suggests.

watchPoints.text: A Little Something jumping — if she makes a jumping error early she loses her tactical advantage entirely and the race shape collapses in favour of Gore Point or White Riot.
White Riot's fall record (F in recent form) is a live safety flag at Stratford's fences on fast ground; Kielan Woods will need to keep him organised from the outset.

Citizen Jane's going — she has run all five of her trackable recent runs on soft or heavy ground and this good-to-firm surface at Stratford is a material step up in ground speed that could find her out.

No Mean Feat returns after 54 days off with a hood on for the first time; watch market moves and early appearance in the paddock as the hood and freshness combined could make him unpredictable at the start or early in the race.

Gore Point's tongue tie fitted for the first time adds a small but genuine unknown for a horse who has otherwise been consistent — monitor his paddock demeanour for signs of comfort or agitation before the off.
